focus: Busan Political Crisis: resolve FRUS 'Yun-Kyong', test the May 24-27 martial-law command chain, and add UN/FRUS cross-provenance

material_findings.finding: The identity left unresolved in pass273 as FRUS 'Yun-Kyong' is now resolved to 윤우경 (尹宇景). The National Institute of Korean History's Korean rendering of the same FRUS editorial note explicitly names 윤우경 as the Chief of National Police appointed immediately before martial law. The Academy of Korean Studies biography independently identifies 윤우경, 1900-1995, as Seoul police chief and then Interior Ministry Chief of National Police in 1952.

Hong Pom-Hi is independently resolved to 홍범희. AKS gives the Hanja as 洪範憙, lifespan 1917-1972, and records a second term as Interior Vice Minister from May to July 1952. This corrects variant Hanja found in some later lists and supplies a biographical node beyond the FRUS romanization.

FRUS telegram 1170 records Rhee's own May 27 account that the cabinet had decided on martial law toward the end of the prior week; when approval was requested he agreed and personally suggested including Pusan. Rhee further said he telephoned Army Chief Lee Jong-chan, that the Defense Minister would issue the decree, Won Yong-deok would be appointed martial-law commander, and Won would take orders directly from the President. This is a contemporaneous diplomatic record of Rhee's own stated command arrangement and materially narrows the martial-law authority chain.

The same telegram records Van Fleet saying neither he nor ROK Army Chief Lee had been informed or consulted in advance of the decision to impose martial law. This creates a precise timing/provenance tension with Rhee's account: Lee may have been contacted only after the cabinet/presidential political decision, for implementation rather than prior consultation. It does not prove Lee participated in the decision to impose martial law.

Rhee showed Van Fleet papers he characterized as Lee's messages to Won and other officers countermanding the prior oral understanding and requiring the martial-law commander to take no action except under Lee's instructions. The papers themselves were not reproduced in the telegram. Their document numbers/originals are now a high-value lead because they could expose the exact conflict between presidential direct-command claims and Army chain-of-command claims.

Rhee told Van Fleet that Lee was implicated in a plot against him and might be removed; Van Fleet defended Lee's political neutrality and suggested Paik Sun-yop if replacement became unavoidable. This is evidence of a civil-military personnel conflict during the crisis, not proof that Lee joined a plot.

UNCURK report A/2187 independently records that So Min-ho was arrested by ROK military police after the May 25 martial-law declaration and transferred to court martial, and reproduces a public notice attributed to the Martial Law Commander. This supplies a UN provenance line separate from FRUS for the So arrest/court-martial sub-event.

FRUS telegram 1200 records the formal US position delivered May 30 that martial law should be lifted in Pusan because the CG EUSAK judged it unnecessary as a military necessity. Rhee replied it would be lifted shortly but defended action against an alleged internal conspiracy. This keeps the military-necessity assessment separate from Rhee's internal-security justification.

FRUS identifies telegram 1164 of May 26 as the UNCURK invitation that brought Van Fleet into the Pusan crisis discussion, and telegram 1196 of May 29 as containing the earlier wording of the US letter later delivered as telegram 1200. Even where the full unprinted telegrams are not online, their numbers, dates, subject role and archival file references are now concrete retrieval targets rather than generic leads.

FRUS editorial note on July 2-4, citing A/2187, records police 'guiding and escorting' absent Assembly members to the special session and the July 4 compromise amendment vote of 163-0 with 3 abstentions among 166 members. This is a later coercion/constitutional sub-event and should not be merged into the May 26 bus detention.

adversarial_checks: Tested whether FRUS 'Yun-Kyong' was an unresolvable romanization; NIHK's Korean FRUS rendering explicitly resolves it to 윤우경 and AKS independently matches the 1952 office.
Did not treat later unofficial police-chief lists as decisive when NIHK and AKS institutional sources were available.
Preserved the one-day ambiguity between May 24 appointment wording and later office lists showing May 25 as term start.
Separated Rhee's reported self-account of the command arrangement from an independently recovered signed order.
Used Van Fleet's statement that Lee was not consulted in advance to test, not erase, Rhee's claim that he later telephoned Lee for implementation.
Did not infer Lee approved the political decision merely because Rhee said Lee agreed to an implementation arrangement.
Did not infer Won ordered individual arrests merely from Rhee's claim that Won would take orders directly from him.
Did not infer Rhee personally ordered So Min-ho's arrest; A/2187 and FRUS corroborate the arrest but the individual arrest instrument remains missing.
Preserved Rhee's allegation that Lee was implicated in a plot as an allegation, paired with Van Fleet's contrary assessment.
Kept the May 26 bus detention distinct from the July 2-4 police escort/coercion of legislators.
Kept US military-necessity assessment distinct from Korean government security justification.
Flagged the Hong Beom-hui Hanja variation rather than silently choosing a later-list spelling over AKS's biographical entry.

history_debt_updates.advance: Rhee's own May 27 reported account now supplies a direct presidential-command claim for the martial-law arrangement and Pusan inclusion, while Van Fleet supplies contrary timing evidence about Lee's prior consultation. This narrows political/command authority but still does not identify the issuer of individual arrest/detention orders.
